analysis: Partition by subscription, resource ID, service and currency. Preserve unattributed charges as a separate bucket. Do not combine currencies or substitute missing rows with zero unless the fully reconciled billing extract establishes a true zero.

For each of the last seven complete days, compute the mean of the preceding 30 complete daily values, excluding the tested day. Calculate delta = observed minus mean and percentage = 100 * delta / mean. Flag absolute percentage above 20; if mean is zero report new spend with percentage null, not infinity.

Require 30 comparable baseline days for the requested test. Mark shorter histories Not assessed for the rolling test and report coverage. Flag provisional billing days separately from confirmed anomalies.
Aggregate the same daily rows by service and currency for service anomalies; do not add resource and service findings as separate spend.

Correlate cost onset with SKU, deployment and write events by resource ID and UTC time. Label causes hypotheses unless a change and its billing effect are demonstrated. Publish amount, direction, baseline, completeness and supporting events.

Activity Log does not prove workload usage or root cause, and Resource Graph may lag resource changes.

validation_cases: Healthy: 37 complete days at 100 currency units produce no deviation findings.
Finding: a tested day at 150 against a 100 baseline produces a 50 absolute and 50 percent increase.

collection.command: az rest --method post --subscription "<subscription_id>" --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<subscription_id>/providers/Microsoft.CostManagement/query?api-version=2025-03-01" --body '{"type":"Usage","timeframe":"Custom","timePeriod":{"from":"<month_start_utc>","to":"<month_end_utc>"},"dataset":{"granularity":"Daily","aggregation":{"totalCost":{"name":"PreTaxCost","function":"Sum"}},"grouping":[{"type":"Dimension","name":"ResourceId"}]}}' --output json

analysis: Classify disks only when managedBy and all shared attachment references are empty and diskState is unattached. For public IPs check ipConfiguration, NAT gateway and other owner references; for NICs check VM and private endpoint ownership; for NSGs check both subnet and NIC association arrays.
For load balancers report zero healthy backends and zero processed bytes over seven complete days as distinct review signals. Require metric coverage and account for internal, HA and standby designs.

For snapshots require an observed creation timestamp older than 90 days and an absent source disk confirmed by a scoped resource read, not merely missing ARG rows. Retention and recovery ownership must be reviewed.

For Application Gateway pools and both Front Door generations require fourteen days of requests with backend/origin attribution. A zero aggregate or missing diagnostic stream does not establish every backend is unused.

For App Service plans distinguish zero assigned apps from all assigned apps stopped. Shared capacity, slots, function apps and restart plans can justify the plan; emit review candidates rather than deletion recommendations.

Join observed monthly cost by normalized resource ID and currency; report candidate_cost separately from confirmed_avoidable_cost. Without owner validation and a feasible removal plan confirmed avoidable cost remains null.
Keep age null when systemData.createdAt or a provider creation field is missing. Enumerate evidence and coverage for each of eight patterns and preserve denied subcases as Not assessed.
limitations: Unattached or idle resources may be recovery assets, reserved endpoints or standby capacity; orphan candidates are not established waste.
Backend metrics, source disk history and creation dates are not universally available. Empty queries and denied reads cannot prove absence.

Flag no applicable budget, no enabled notifications, or all enabled actual cost thresholds above 100 percent. Report exactly 100 percent separately as at limit, not above it. Distinguish forecast alerts from actual alerts.
Inspect recipient/action group references and missing destinations without sending a test notification. A configured address alone does not prove successful delivery.

analysis: Group assignments by principal object ID and normalized scope ancestry. An identical role at an ancestor is a redundancy candidate only when ancestor access is active, conditions are equivalent and the child adds no distinct delegated or temporal semantics.

For different roles compare effective action sets after wildcard expansion and NotActions subtraction separately for control and data planes. Role names or an Owner/Contributor/Reader ranking are not a sufficient containment test.

Identify multiple same principal same scope assignments and calculate their permission union. Recommend consolidation only if a candidate role preserves required access without introducing unrelated permissions.

For Owner or Contributor compare observed successful operations with approved workload requirements and narrower built in roles. List unobserved but required actions and missing telemetry. Never infer least privilege from 30 days with no write events.

Treat PIM eligibility, group membership, deny assignments and ABAC conditions as separate dependencies; if not collected, declare effective access Partial. Never remove assignments during the assessment.
Report principal ID/type, display name when independently resolved, assignment IDs, roles, scopes, overlap proof and the owner validation required for any access change.
limitations: Activity Log does not record all reads or data plane usage, and no activity does not establish unnecessary access.
PIM, nested groups, deny assignments and conditional permissions can invalidate simple role containment conclusions.

objective: Map a precisely specified Azure operation to required permissions and the narrowest suitable role, emitting a local custom role draft when no exact built in match exists.

inputs.name: subscription_id
inputs.description: Validated approved subscription UUID.

inputs.name: scope_id
inputs.description: Validated intended assignment scope within the approved subscription.

inputs.name: provider_namespace
inputs.description: Provider namespace matching the requested operation, validated against a provider read, such as Microsoft.Compute.

inputs.description: Concrete user operation, target type and control/data plane. Ambiguous descriptions must not produce a definitive minimum role.

inputs.description: Reviewed compact JSON array of exact operation names confirmed against provider metadata. Before source substitution the host enforces every string against [A-Za-z0-9.]+/[A-Za-z0-9./]+, rejecting quotes, backslashes and wildcard operations.

inputs.name: required_data_actions_json
inputs.description: Reviewed compact JSON array of exact data plane permissions, or []. Before source substitution the host enforces the same exact operation grammar as required_actions_json.

inputs.name: artifact_path
inputs.description: Approved relative new file path such as artifacts\permissions\custom-role-draft.json. Before source substitution the host permits only letters, digits, underscores, periods, hyphens and path separators, rejects parent traversal and absolute paths, and verifies workspace containment and no existing file. collection.command: az provider operation show --subscription "<subscription_id>" --namespace "<provider_namespace>" --output json
collection.explanation: Match exact provider operation names and isDataAction where returned. Operation display text alone is not proof of all permissions required by a compound workflow.

collection.command: az role definition list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --scope "<scope_id>" --output json
collection.explanation: Retain roleType, permissions and assignable scopes. Include built in and custom roles in evidence, but identify built in candidates explicitly.

collection.name: Local minimum permission draft
collection.command:
import json, re, uuid
from pathlib import Path
root = Path.cwd().resolve()
p = (root / '<artifact_path>').resolve()
assert root in p.parents and not p.exists() and '<' not in str(p)
scope = '<scope_id>'
assert re.fullmatch(r'/subscriptions/[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}(?:/resourceGroups/[A-Za-z0-9_.()-]+)?(?:/providers/[A-Za-z0-9_./()-]+)?', scope)
uuid.UUID(scope.split('/')[2])
parts = scope.split('/')
assignable_scope = '/'.join(parts[:5]) if len(parts) >= 5 and parts[3].lower() == 'resourcegroups' else '/'.join(parts[:3])
actions = json.loads('<required_actions_json>')
data_actions = json.loads('<required_data_actions_json>')
assert isinstance(actions, list) and isinstance(data_actions, list) and actions + data_actions
assert all(isinstance(a, str) and re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9.]+/[A-Za-z0-9./]+', a) for a in actions + data_actions)
draft = {'Name': 'Scoped operation role draft', 'IsCustom': True, 'Description': 'Review before creation. Intended assignment scope: ' + scope, 'Actions': actions, 'NotActions': [], 'DataActions': data_actions, 'NotDataActions': [], 'AssignableScopes': [assignable_scope]}
p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
with p.open('x', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
    json.dump(draft, handle, indent=2)
collection.explanation: Run only after matching supplied arrays to provider metadata and reviewing dependencies. The definition's assignable scope is the enclosing resource group or subscription; the intended assignment can still be the narrower resource scope. Creates a local JSON proposal only. Host enforcement must restrict paths, prohibit role writes and substitute validated JSON arrays as escaped data rather than arbitrary source text.

analysis: Translate the stated operation into exact provider actions, distinguishing control plane and data plane. For multi step workflows enumerate dependent read and action permissions; if documentation or evidence is missing return an incomplete mapping rather than claim a minimum.
Expand candidate role wildcard permissions against provider operation metadata and subtract NotActions and NotDataActions in their own planes. These exclusions are not deny assignments.
Keep roles that cover all required actions and are assignable at the target scope. Rank by excess permission count and scope breadth, reporting ties and any sensitive unrelated grants.

If no exact built in permission match exists, generate the reviewed local custom role JSON with only confirmed actions and narrow assignable scope. An existing broader role can be an alternative but must be labeled broader.
Check ABAC conditions, deny assignments, resource locks, PIM and provider specific authorization independently. A matching role is not proof the caller can execute the operation.

Validate JSON syntax and compare the draft permission set against the approved action list. An administrator must review and approve creation and assignment separately; this workflow executes neither.
limitations: Provider operation metadata does not document every prerequisite for compound tasks or service data plane policies.
Role coverage does not override locks, deny assignments, conditions or PIM activation requirements.

analysis: Resolve each assigned principal using the correct approved tenant and type. Only a repeatable authorized 404 after replication delay is an orphan candidate; 403, timeout and foreign principal ambiguity are unknown.

For service principals calculate last successful and last observed sign in from both application and managed identity exports, with table coverage and retention. No events in a partial or short retention window is insufficient to claim 90 day inactivity.

Separate no successful sign in observed, last success older than 90 days and principal deleted. Preserve groups as not applicable for user sign in checks; stale user checks do not apply to group objects.

Minimize personal names in customer summaries and retain raw sign in evidence only in the approved local evidence location.

collection.command: az monitor log-analytics query --subscription "<subscription_id>" --workspace "<workspace_id>" --timespan "<start_utc>/<end_utc>" --analytics-query "union isfuzzy=true (AZKVAuditLogs | where TimeGenerated >= datetime(<start_utc>) and TimeGenerated < datetime(<end_utc>) | where _SubscriptionId == '<subscription_id>' | where OperationName in~ ('SecretGet','SecretList') | project TimeGenerated, source='KeyVaultDataPlane', operation=tostring(OperationName), target=tostring(_ResourceId), identity=tostring(Identity), result=tostring(ResultType)), (AzureActivity | where TimeGenerated >= datetime(<start_utc>) and TimeGenerated < datetime(<end_utc>) | where ResourceId =~ '/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<management_group_id>' or tolower(ResourceId) startswith tolower('/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<management_group_id>/') | project TimeGenerated, source='ManagementGroupExport', operation=OperationNameValue, target=ResourceId, identity=Caller, result=ActivityStatusValue) | order by TimeGenerated asc" --output json
collection.explanation: Execute the management group branch only if the optional group was explicitly approved, otherwise remove that branch before submission. Repeat by individually approved group ID when auditing multiple nodes; group IDs are not hierarchical paths. Validate log schema and exported diagnostic coverage first. Missing tables, fuzzy warnings and ingestion gaps are Not assessed. Never read secret values.

analysis: Select roleAssignments/write and delete, policyAssignments/write and delete, subscription scoped Microsoft.Resources/deployments/write and managementGroups write/delete operations using normalized operationName.value and the target's exact scope.
Report success, failure and started events distinctly. Correlate lifecycle events by correlationId and target rather than counting each as a separate completed change.
Key Vault SecretGet is data plane evidence from resource logs, not subscription Activity Log. Include result and caller identity where present without exposing request content or secret material.
Management group changes outside the subscription require their own approved export. Do not claim a subscription Activity Log scan covers tenant hierarchy changes.
Compare collected events with owner approved change windows and actor allowlists; unusual events are review findings, not proof of malicious intent.
Record observation bounds, collection latency and inaccessible sources so a quiet period with no export cannot be represented as no privileged activity.
limitations: Activity Log generally excludes data plane reads such as secret access and may arrive after a collection run.
Management group and Key Vault event coverage depends on preexisting export configuration and authorized workspace access.

objective: Compute a transparent customer defined hygiene index with six weighted evidence components and explicit unknown coverage.

inputs.name: subscription_id
inputs.description: Validated approved subscription UUID.

inputs.name: resource_id
inputs.description: Validated eligible resource ID for diagnostic setting reads.

collection.explanation: Repeat per eligible resource. Check required enabled categories or category groups and valid destination references. Presence alone does not prove delivery.

collection.name: Policy and Defender evidence
collection.command:
az policy state summarize --subscription "<subscription_id>" --output json
az security secure-scores list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --output json
collection.explanation: Preserve evaluated resource counts, exempt/unknown states and score identity. Use the classic Azure secure score returned by this API, not the separate risk based Defender portal model.

analysis: Compute component ratios from eligible assessed denominators: compliant tags 20 percent, effective locks 15 percent, required enabled alert coverage 20 percent, qualifying diagnostics 15 percent, policy compliance 15 percent and classic Defender score 15 percent.

For tags, locks, alerts and diagnostics count fully passing resources divided by eligible resources under coverage_policy. Expand alert scope or tag based criteria before counting; diagnostic settings must include required categories and a valid destination.

For policy use compliant divided by compliant plus noncompliant evaluated eligible resources, with exemptions and unknown states separately listed. For Defender use returned current/max only when max is positive and the selected initiative is identified.

Calculate total score = 100 * sum(weight * component_ratio) only when all applicable components are assessed. For unavailable components provide a known contribution lower bound and potential upper bound, but total score null; do not renormalize missing evidence into a pass.

If a component has no eligible resources, require a documented customer policy for not applicable weighting; otherwise keep the aggregate unassessed. This is a customer hygiene index, not an official Azure score.
For complete totals below 70 rank improvements by lost weighted points and action effort. For incomplete totals prioritize evidence gaps before score based conclusions.
limitations: This composite index is not an official Azure compliance or security score and depends on the agreed coverage policy.
The classic Azure secure score differs from the risk based Cloud Secure Score, and diagnostic configuration does not establish successful log delivery.

assert isinstance(ids, list) and ids and all(isinstance(i, str) and i.lower().startswith(prefix.lower()) and '<' not in i for i in ids)
body = {'resources': ids, 'targetResourceGroup': f'/subscriptions/{target}/resourceGroups/{target_rg}'}
draft = {'status': 'DraftNotExecuted', 'validation_method': 'POST', 'validation_url': f'https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{source}/resourceGroups/{source_rg}/validateMoveResources?api-version=2021-04-01', 'validation_body': body, 'move_cli_arguments_never_executed': ['az', 'resource', 'move', '--subscription', source, '--destination-subscription-id', target, '--destination-group', target_rg, '--ids'] + ids, 'approval_required': True, 'validation_result': None, 'rollback': 'Review reverse move feasibility, backup and restoration before approval; reverse move is not guaranteed.'}
p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
with p.open('x', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
    json.dump(draft, handle, indent=2)
collection.explanation: Only writes the local draft. It does not submit even the server validation action. Validate approved IDs and safe JSON substitution in the host. Do not use az resource move --validate-only, which is not the documented move validation interface. analysis: Verify both subscriptions are active and in the same tenant. Confirm each top level type supports the requested cross subscription move using current official move support and service specific guidance; reject unknown support.

Build dependency closure from provider references, including shared networking, disks and nested resources. Exclude child resources from the explicit top level move list where they move with parents. Unknown dependencies block a Ready recommendation.

Compare target inherited policy effects, required tags and deny conditions, resource ID changes, source scoped role assignments and target inherited access. Role assignments do not simply transfer with moved resource IDs.

Generate only the local draft containing exact source, target, selected resources, validation request and never executed move arguments. Validation is a separate privileged action and the read workflow must not call it.

Validation success is not a completed move.

collection.name: Local classic or policy proposal with deployment text only
collection.command:
import json, ipaddress, re, uuid
from pathlib import Path
root = Path.cwd().resolve()
p = (root / '<artifact_path>').resolve()
bicep_path = p.with_suffix('.bicep')
assert root in p.parents and '<' not in str(p) and not p.exists() and not bicep_path.exists() and p != bicep_path
sub = str(uuid.UUID('<subscription_id>'))
rg, fw, name, coll = '<resource_group>', '<firewall_name>', '<rule_name>', '<collection_name>'
mode, policy, policy_rg, group = '<management_mode>', '<policy_name>', '<policy_resource_group>', '<group_name>'
assert mode in ('classic', 'policy')
assert all(re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,80}', v) for v in (rg, fw, name, coll, policy, policy_rg, group))
assert re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9]+-(?:inbound|outbound)-[A-Za-z0-9]+', name)
protocol = '<protocol>'.upper()
assert protocol in ('TCP', 'UDP')
source = str(ipaddress.ip_network('<source_cidr>', strict=True))
assert ipaddress.ip_network(source).prefixlen > 0
destination = '<destination>'
is_fqdn = False
try:
    destination = str(ipaddress.ip_network(destination, strict=False))
    assert ipaddress.ip_network(destination).prefixlen > 0
except ValueError:
    assert len(destination) <= 253 and re.fullmatch(r'(?:[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?\.)+[A-Za-z]{2,63}', destination)
    destination = destination.lower()
    is_fqdn = True
    assert '<dns_proxy_verified>'.lower() == 'true'
ports = '<ports>'.split(',')
for port in ports:
    assert re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+(?:-[0-9]+)?', port)
    bounds = [int(v) for v in port.split('-')]
    assert all(1 <= v <= 65535 for v in bounds) and bounds[0] <= bounds[-1]
priority = int('<priority>')
assert 100 <= priority <= 65000
destination_key = 'destinationFqdns' if is_fqdn else 'destinationAddresses'
rule = {'name': name, 'sourceAddresses': [source], destination_key: [destination], 'destinationPorts': ports}
def json_expression(value):
    return "json('''\n" + json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n''')"
if mode == 'classic':
    rule['protocols'] = [protocol]
    collection = {'name': coll, 'properties': {'priority': priority, 'action': {'type': 'Allow'}, 'rules': [rule]}}
    cli = ['az', 'network', 'firewall', 'network-rule', 'create', '--subscription', sub, '--resource-group', rg, '--firewall-name', fw, '--collection-name', coll, '--name', name, '--protocols', protocol, '--source-addresses', source, '--destination-fqdns' if is_fqdn else '--destination-addresses', destination, '--destination-ports'] + ports + ['--action', 'Allow', '--priority', str(priority)]
    bicep = '// DRAFT FRAGMENT. Merge into the complete existing firewall properties, preserving every existing collection.\nvar proposedNetworkRuleCollections = ' + json_expression([collection]) + '\noutput reviewedCollections array = proposedNetworkRuleCollections\n'
else:
    assert 'not-applicable' not in (policy, policy_rg, group)
    rule.update({'ruleType': 'NetworkRule', 'ipProtocols': [protocol]})
    collection = {'name': coll, 'priority': priority, 'ruleCollectionType': 'FirewallPolicyFilterRuleCollection', 'action': {'type': 'Allow'}, 'rules': [rule]}
    props = {'priority': priority, 'ruleCollections': [collection]}
    bicep = "// DRAFT ONLY. New group name must be unused. Existing groups are not replaced.\nresource policy 'Microsoft.Network/firewallPolicies@2024-05-01' existing = {\n  name: '" + policy + "'\n}\nresource proposedGroup 'Microsoft.Network/firewallPolicies/ruleCollectionGroups@2024-05-01' = {\n  parent: policy\n  name: '" + group + "'\n  properties: " + json_expression(props) + '\n}\n'
    cli = ['az', 'deployment', 'group', 'create', '--subscription', sub, '--resource-group', policy_rg, '--template-file', str(bicep_path)]
draft = {'status': 'DraftNotExecuted', 'target_mode': mode, 'rule': rule, 'collection': collection, 'cli_never_executed': cli, 'bicep_artifact': str(bicep_path.relative_to(root)), 'bicep_content': bicep, 'validation_required': ['Match observed management mode and attached policy scope', 'Check routes, inherited rules and all priority/name collisions', 'Verify DNS proxy and application rule suitability for FQDN', 'Compile Bicep locally and review complete deployment diff', 'Obtain separate flow test, deployment and rollback approval'], 'approval_required': True}
p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
with bicep_path.open('x', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
    handle.write(bicep)
with p.open('x', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
    json.dump(draft, handle, indent=2)
collection.explanation: Only creates local JSON and sibling Bicep files, never runs the stored CLI arguments. The policy branch adds a reviewed new collection group to the observed existing policy; classic Bicep is an explicitly labeled merge fragment, not a partial firewall deployment. Validate all supplied tokens and safely escape substitutions in the host before running. Existing files, unresolved inputs and unsupported scopes fail closed.

analysis: Validate source CIDR against the observed subnet, destination against the owner approved target and ports/protocol against the application requirement. Reject wildcard destinations, broad source networks and unresolved placeholders.

Determine classic versus policy management and inspect inherited policy/rule collections, DNAT precedence, overlapping allows/denies and occupied priorities. A new allow cannot override an earlier matching deny.
Confirm the source route traverses this firewall and return traffic has a viable route. A rule proposal does not establish that traffic will reach the firewall.

Generate the local collection for the exact approved TCP or UDP flow using literal IP/CIDR or FQDN fields as appropriate. FQDN network rules require verified DNS proxy and no wildcard; prefer an application rule for HTTP/S or MSSQL when its protocol semantics are required.
Preserve all existing rule collections when integrating Bicep. The fragment is not a complete firewall resource and must never replace the current rule array unreviewed.

Require local Bicep compile, reviewed deployment diff, owner approval, bounded positive and negative flow tests, monitoring and rollback to the recorded prior rule configuration before any separately authorized deployment.
limitations: The local draft supports TCP/UDP network rules and same subscription policy targets. Cross subscription policy scope, ICMP and application rules require a separately reviewed adaptation.
Firewall configuration, routing, DNS proxy and precedence must be validated together; generating a rule is not proof of allowed connectivity.

analysis: Rank denied network tuples by log hit count, preserving source, destination, port and protocol. Denial counts are not unique connections and must not be labeled as such.
Analyze all internal source denials against customer CIDRs, not just RFC1918 or the overall top twenty. Correlate approved application flows before suggesting a misconfiguration.
Join allowed IP/FQDN hits to approved indicators with source timestamp and expiration. Report false positive review and do not infer suspiciousness from an arbitrary destination list.

Report hourly hit counts per rule collection, action and table. Per collection traffic bytes remain null because these tables do not contain payload byte counts; present aggregate DataProcessed separately.

Verify log category coverage, table plan, diagnostic destination, observation bounds and partial query warnings. If legacy mode is configured, report that the supplied resource specific queries cannot assess those records until a separately verified legacy parser is supplied.
Recommend narrowly scoped rule or application owner review, never automatically add allow rules, block indicators or change diagnostic routing.
limitations: Resource specific rule logs report rule hits rather than complete flow payload volume; per collection network bytes cannot be derived from _BilledSize.
Logging mode, table plan and retention can limit coverage; an empty or missing table is not evidence of no traffic.

collection.explanation: These are ARM certificate reference metadata, not Key Vault secret value retrieval. Inspect certificate type, secret version/reference and deployment state. Managed certificate expiry not returned by the API stays null; renewal ownership is reported separately.

collection.name: API Management certificate and hostname metadata
collection.command:
az rest --method get --subscription "<subscription_id>" --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<subscription_id>/resourceGroups/<resource_group>/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/<apim_name>/certificates?api-version=2024-05-01" --output json
az apim show --subscription "<subscription_id>" --resource-group "<resource_group>" --name "<apim_name>" --output json
collection.explanation: Follow nextLink for the certificate collection. Collection properties include subject, thumbprint and expirationDate, but not a universal issuer field. Service hostnameConfigurations cover gateway TLS bindings separately from client/backend certificates.

collection.name: Parse public X509 metadata locally
collection.explanation: Local parsing of public DER only. Other services' observed publicCertData can use the same X509 constructor after a documented metadata adapter; if the service does not expose the public certificate, subject or issuer stays null rather than being guessed.

analysis: Inventory and report coverage for all five families, separating stored certificates, installed certificates and active listener/domain bindings.

Resolve each binding to its exact certificate thumbprint or version. A versionless vault reference may auto rotate, but verify actual deployment metadata and do not infer rotation succeeded from a newer stored version.
Use public certificate parsing or authoritative returned expirationDate/attributes metadata. Do not substitute certificate policy issuer provider name for the actual X509 issuer.

Compute fractional days remaining from expiry UTC minus assessment_utc. Classify expired below zero, expiring within 30 days inclusive, and later otherwise. A null expiry is Not assessed, not healthy.

For Front Door managed/classic certificates with no exposed expiry record platform renewal ownership and deployment state but retain expiry null. Do not equate provisioning success with a fresh served certificate.

Deduplicate certificate versions by thumbprint for inventory counts while retaining all affected bindings. Recommend owner renewal and post renewal binding verification, with no secret access or live endpoint probes in this read workflow.
limitations: Some managed Front Door or secret only certificates do not expose expiry/public DER through these metadata APIs; unknown fields stay null.
Stored certificate expiry does not prove which certificate is currently served on every endpoint, and automatic renewal must not be assumed successful.

objective: Assess DDoS Network and IP Protection coverage for public facing VNet resources and provide cost estimates only from approved rate evidence.

inputs.name: subscription_id
inputs.description: Validated approved subscription UUID.

inputs.name: resource_id
inputs.description: Validated approved VNet, public IP or DDoS plan ARM ID for authoritative reads.

inputs.name: rate_evidence
inputs.description: Optional approved current list or contracted rate evidence with exact SKU, meter, region, currency, unit, included IP count and timestamp. Unknown prices remain null.

permissions.scope: Approved VNets, public IPs and DDoS plans
permissions.purpose: Read protection associations and public exposure without enabling plans.

collection.name: Network and IP protection configuration
collection.command:
az network vnet list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --output json
az network public-ip list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --output json
collection.explanation: Retain VNet enableDdosProtection/ddosProtectionPlan and public IP ddosSettings including protectionMode and plan references when present. The historical name Standard must not hide the current Network versus IP Protection distinction.

collection.name: Public resource placement and plan inventory
collection.command: az graph query --subscriptions "<subscription_id>" --first 1000 -q "Resources | where type in~ ('microsoft.network/networkinterfaces','microsoft.network/loadbalancers','microsoft.network/applicationgateways','microsoft.network/natgateways','microsoft.network/azurefirewalls','microsoft.network/virtualnetworkgateways','microsoft.network/bastionhosts','microsoft.network/ddosprotectionplans') | project id, name, type, resourceGroup, properties, sku" --output json
collection.explanation: Page with --skip-token from skipToken. Join PIP ID to actual frontend/NIC owner and owner subnet/VNet. Load balancer backends are not a single VNet association unless its actual frontend/backends establish it.

collection.name: Confirm candidate protection state
collection.command: az resource show --subscription "<subscription_id>" --ids "<resource_id>" --output json
collection.explanation: Confirm relevant VNet, PIP and plan metadata before a coverage verdict. Explicitly scoped external plan references require additional approval; a missing plan read is unknown, not no protection.

analysis: Build public facing resource counts per VNet by resolving public frontend and NIC subnet references, including Application Gateway. Count distinct public owners and PIPs separately.

Evaluate VNet Network Protection enabled plus a valid associated plan, and evaluate explicit public IP protection mode independently. IP Protection can cover an individual eligible PIP without a VNet Network Protection plan.

Flag public facing resources without demonstrated enhanced protection as customer policy review findings, while distinguishing platform infrastructure protection from Network/IP Protection. Unsupported resource/PIP SKUs require documented eligibility checks.
Do not automatically flag an entire VNet as uncovered when all eligible public IPs have IP Protection. Show per PIP coverage, VNet plan coverage and mixed coverage separately.

Estimate plan or IP Protection incremental monthly cost only from rate_evidence, considering already paid shared plans, included quantities and overages. Do not multiply a shared plan base price by every VNet.

When rates or allocation are unknown output estimate null and request a rate verification. Recommendations must consider security benefits and existing shared coverage rather than claim guaranteed savings.
limitations: Public endpoint eligibility and DDoS feature scope differ by resource and public IP SKU; configuration must not be generalized across every PaaS endpoint.
A shared plan has included quantities and allocation constraints, so missing rate evidence prevents a reliable incremental cost estimate.

objective: Assess public and private A, AAAA and CNAME records with scoped resource ownership and resolver evidence while avoiding false dangling DNS claims.

inputs.name: subscription_id
inputs.description: Approved subscription UUID; repeat only for explicit approved subscriptions.

inputs.name: resource_group
inputs.description: Validated group of the selected DNS zone.

inputs.name: zone_name
inputs.description: Validated exact public or private DNS zone name from inventory.

inputs.name: target_resource_id
inputs.description: Validated ARM targetResource.id from a real alias record; other subscriptions need separate approval.

inputs.name: fqdn
inputs.description: Validated exact CNAME target or record FQDN approved for DNS lookup, no wildcards or arbitrary command text.

inputs.name: dns_server
inputs.description: Approved resolver IP literal reachable from the intended public or private network vantage. No assumed resolver context.

inputs.name: artifact_path
inputs.description: Approved relative new JSON path such as artifacts/dns/resolution-evidence.json within the workspace.

inputs.name: external_target_allowlist
inputs.description: Customer approved external/on premises IPs, domains and cross subscription target exceptions with ownership evidence.

permissions.scope: Approved public/private DNS zones and target resources
permissions.purpose: Read records and alias targets; DNS query egress is separately host allowlisted to the approved resolver.

collection.name: Public and private DNS zone inventories
collection.command:
az network dns zone list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --output json
az network private-dns zone list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --output json
collection.explanation: Build separate zone family denominators. Zone names can overlap across split horizon contexts; retain zone ARM ID, not name alone.

collection.name: Public and private zone records
collection.command:
az network dns record-set list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --resource-group "<resource_group>" --zone-name "<zone_name>" --output json
az network private-dns record-set list --subscription "<subscription_id>" --resource-group "<resource_group>" --zone-name "<zone_name>" --output json
collection.explanation: Execute only the appropriate family command for each inventoried zone, not both blindly. Retain A/AAAA/CNAME records, targetResource alias IDs, TTL and metadata. Record deleted or inaccessible zones separately.

collection.name: Known in scope IP ownership
collection.command: az graph query --subscriptions "<subscription_id>" --first 1000 -q "Resources | where type in~ ('microsoft.network/publicipaddresses','microsoft.network/networkinterfaces','microsoft.network/loadbalancers','microsoft.network/applicationgateways','microsoft.network/privateendpoints') | project id, name, type, resourceGroup, properties" --output json
collection.explanation: Page using --skip-token from skipToken. Build IPv4 and IPv6 ownership maps from observed public/private address fields; the map is not a universal global IP ownership database.

collection.name: Authoritative alias target existence
collection.command: az resource show --subscription "<subscription_id>" --ids "<target_resource_id>" --output json
collection.explanation: Only follow a target within approved scope; select an explicitly approved target subscription for cross subscription reads. Preserve 404 versus 403 and transient failure; a graph miss alone is not deleted target evidence.

collection.name: Approved resolver query and local evidence
collection.explanation: Only run from an approved resolver vantage with host enforced domain/resolver allowlists. Uses Windows DNS client and writes local evidence. An error is not automatically NXDOMAIN: distinguish authoritative no such name from timeout, SERVFAIL or refused using the recorded error and resolver evidence.

analysis: Normalize DNS names and IP literals, preserving zone ID, family, record type and TTL. Parse A/AAAA with an IP library and compare exact IPs to the complete approved ownership map.

An IP not in current approved Azure inventory is unmatched, not necessarily dangling: check external_target_allowlist, on premises ownership, other approved subscriptions and service managed endpoints before raising a deletion candidate.

Resolve CNAME chains through the approved resolver, detect loops and bound chain depth. A response from the wrong DNS vantage does not establish private record failure; record timeout/refused/SERVFAIL separately from NXDOMAIN.
For alias targetResource IDs use an authorized resource read. Repeatable 404 can establish a missing target candidate, while 403 and unapproved cross subscription targets remain unknown.
Azure alias records can become empty record sets when a supported target is deleted; report empty alias sets separately instead of assuming a stale nonempty target pointer always remains.
Recommend owner verification and TTL aware change planning. Never delete records, mutate aliases or treat one transient resolution failure as proof of a takeover vulnerability.
limitations: Approved subscription IP inventory cannot prove global ownership or absence of on premises/external targets.
Private DNS resolution depends on the network vantage, forwarding and links, and transient resolver errors are not deleted resource evidence.
